The original test source is retained as test_fingering.py.txt (data, never
imported or executed). cases.json contains its eight literal input/expected
fixtures. Conversion used Python's standard-library AST parser and a restricted
literal-data reader; it did not import, eval or execute upstream code.

Our TypeScript adapter assigns quarter-note durations to the duration-free
examples, retains explicit rests as restBefore, and maps supplied finger numbers
to hard constraints. Six monophonic cases are checked against the actual selected
fingers. Two chord cases are retained as reference data for a future whole-hand
planner; current tests explicitly reject feeding a chord to the single-note API.
These two data/eligibility checks do not claim chord-generation support.

The upstream algorithm cites Blake West's performer. No upstream algorithm,
cost database, runtime dependency or installation script was imported or run.
